saints.name: St. Thomas Becket
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The chancellor turned archbishop of Canterbury, who defended the Church's liberty against his king and was murdered at his own altar…
biography: Born in 1118 in Cheapside, London, the son of a Norman merchant, Thomas entered the household of Archbishop Theobald of Canterbury, who made him archdeacon and sent him to study canon law at Bologna and Auxerre. In 1155 Henry II made him chancellor of England.

In 1162 Henry had him made archbishop of Canterbury, expecting a compliant prelate; instead Thomas resigned the chancellorship, embraced austerity, and defended the Church's liberties, above all the immunity of clergy from the king's courts. Condemned at Northampton in 1164, he fled to six years of exile in France.

Reconciled with Henry at Fréteval in July 1170, he returned to Canterbury that December, still refusing to absolve the bishops who had defied him; on 29 December four knights cut him down in his cathedral as the monks sang Vespers. Within days miracles were reported at his tomb, and in 1173 Alexander III declared him a saint.

His shrine at Canterbury drew pilgrims from all Europe for three centuries, until Henry VIII destroyed it in 1538 and struck his name from the service books. Because he gave his life defending the clergy's freedom from the crown, he is honoured as the patron of the secular clergy.
saints.knownFor: Martyred archbishop who defended the liberty of the Church.

canonization.canonized: Canonized in 1173 by Pope Alexander III

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 29 December
